action: General advice: organisations with staff or customers in Jordan should expect Telegram to be unreachable. The Public Security Directorate urges avoiding links from unknown sources and reporting illegal content through official channels.
date_note: Roya News and Al Jazeera, both published 16 November, say the directorate announced the block on Monday (16 November); IDN Times (19 November) gives the same day.
exec: Telegram is blocked across Jordan with no stated end date, which affects any business that reaches staff or customers there through the app.
plain: Jordan has blocked the Telegram messaging app across the country, saying it wants to stop extremist content, extortion and cybercrime. No end date was stated.

sources.name: IDN Times: Cegah Konten Radikal dan Kejahatan Siber, Yordania Blokir Telegram

summary: Jordan's Public Security Directorate announced on Monday 16 November that it had blocked the Telegram app nationwide, Roya News, Al Jazeera and IDN Times report, citing cybercrime, extremism, extortion, threats and risks to national security. IDN Times says authorities have not confirmed how long the block will last. Al Jazeera reports Iraq's media and communications authority also blocked Telegram, giving the company 30 days to comply.

evidence.quote: It gave the company 30 days to comply, without spelling out what would happen after that.

title: Jordan blocks Telegram nationwide, citing extremism and cybercrime

validation.note: Roya News (Jordan) and Al Jazeera each report the Public Security Directorate's announcement of the block; IDN Times relays it via Daily Sabah. The directorate's own statement was not read. The no-end-date point is IDN Times' only; the Iraq block is Al Jazeera's only.

review.note: action advice: was unsourced 'No action needed' plus own advice, now General advice plus the directorate's advice; stronger than source: 'no end date' now 'not confirmed how long' (IDN Times), '30 days to address non-compliant content' now '30 days to comply' (Al Jazeera)
